settings.normal_view: x1 / 9m height, evaluated independently of initial x2

comparison_regions.observation: Normal ×1 uses the unchanged T02 9m orthographic height; the previous 12m wide view and 4.5m initial close view did not establish this scale. At 384×216 the Adventurer reads as a humanoid with a bun/head, torso, two arms and separated boots. Fine facial features and armor engraving merge into a few pixels. Recognition and detail bounds still need human review; diagnostic ×2 is not acceptance evidence. Geometry, 1.8m height and source pose are unchanged.

The same fourteen measured placements and eleven exports remain: small containers/produce/stool below the 1.8m actor, barrels about half its height, canopy/house/birch larger. The barrel has simpler broad bands and an opening; the character has much more high-frequency ornament. Enlarged paving repeats reduce competing surface noise without adding scenery.

Bases/supports and character footprint remain unchanged. The lower lateral key creates more legible cast-shadow direction and blue shadow versus warm lit paving. The original flat receiver repeats the same maps over 4m instead of 2m; this is an explicit reversible presentation deviation. No AO/contact-depth or detailed collision certification is claimed.

Lower ambient/fill and a lateral key retain source hues while making warm/cool lighting and shadow masses clearer. Original PBR maps and authored metal/roughness response remain; detailed normal/metal highlights still undersample. There is no toon banding, outline/highlight pass, atmosphere or final palette treatment.

proposed_bounds.bound: At normal ×1 (9m height, 384×216), identify head/hair, torso, arms and two boots as a complete humanoid with a clear ground silhouette. Review native gameplay pixels, not enlarged diagnostic ×2 or the full-resolution PBR image. Fine facial/armor detail is currently limited and requires an explicit accepted deviation or later T05/BW-098 improvement.

Use physically sensible scene proportions: character 1.8m; small items 0.25–0.5m; barrels 0.85–0.9m; canopy 2.8m; house 4.8m; birch 5.2m. Pose precedes measurement; uniform scaling preserves proportions. Bases contact ground/support and the character footprint stays clear. Normal/diagnostic focus heights are both 1.0m; the 9m/4.5m heights match T02 zooms. Reset remains close/day/135°.

The Adventurer silhouette remains separable from paving, the house and foliage in all three lighting states. Boots and building foundations meet the ground; architecture depth stays visible and amber light preserves character part separation.

T04/T09 must show no stationary pixel changes, no repeated crawl/shimmer on rigid edges during slow/diagonal tracking, no one-frame silhouette disappearance or outline-width pumping. One internal-pixel silhouette lines and selective convex highlights are reviewed in T05. No motion pass is claimed in T03.
No filled-surface outlines, stale reflection/depth frames, actor disappearance or unauthorized information in later combined cases; fallback deviations need explicit review.

Source graphs and virtual-texture readbacks produced black or white exports. Unsaved PBR materials and unsaved conventional texture duplicates transfer the original authored maps per slot, while preserving original material samplers. Export limitations remain explicit.

Normal ×1 returns to the established T02 9m height. Diagnostic ×2 is 4.5m; both focus at 1m. Reset deliberately retains the existing close/day/135° state. The review evaluates normal ×1 separately.
